headline: Gambia to Compensate Abuse Victims Using Dictator's Seized Fortune
meta_description: The Gambia will use $2.5 million from the US sale of ex-ruler Yahya Jammeh's Maryland mansion to pay victims of his 22-year regime.
summary_short: After a US court seized and sold former dictator Yahya Jammeh's Maryland mansion, The Gambia's Reparations Commission received $2.5 million to compensate survivors of hi…
body:
The Gambia's Reparations Commission has received $2.5 million from the sale of a Maryland mansion that once belonged to Yahya Jammeh, the former ruler whose two-decade grip on power ended in 2017. The funds will now go directly to victims and survivors of his regime—people who endured documented human rights abuses, forced disappearances, and extrajudicial killings. A commission of inquiry determined that between 240 and 250 Gambians and foreign nationals lost their lives at the hands of the state or its agents during Jammeh's rule. The money represents tangible restitution for survivors, a rare instance of illicitly gained assets being returned to those harmed.

Jammeh lost the 2016 election to Adama Barrow but initially rejected the results, prompting international intervention. Troops from Senegal and other West African nations were deployed before Jammeh agreed to step down and eventually fled into exile in Equatorial Guinea. Once investigators examined his holdings, they uncovered a staggering pattern of theft: Jammeh owned 281 properties across The Gambia alone, plus additional real estate in the US and Morocco, and controlled over 100 bank accounts. The scale of his appropriation exceeded $300 million—riches impossible to justify on a president's salary.

The US court system determined in 2022 that the Maryland mansion had been purchased with criminal proceeds and misappropriated Gambian public funds, securing the legal right to sell it. The Reparations Commission has pledged to manage the proceeds responsibly and transparently, keeping the needs and rights of survivors at the centre of its work. For a nation still healing from decades of systematic abuse, this recovered money offers both practical support and symbolic acknowledgment that stolen wealth can be reclaimed and redirected toward justice.
quick_facts: $2.5 million received from sale of Jammeh's Maryland mansion
Jammeh fled to Equatorial Guinea after stepping down in 2017
Over $300 million in misappropriated funds discovered
US court seized mansion in 2022 as criminal proceeds
